module_title: Plains and Plateaus - Geomorphology and Mountain Ranges
introduction: At this level, we divide the Northern Plains based on soil relief features and explore the specific mountain ranges (Aravallis, Vindhyas, Satpuras) that border the Peninsular Plateau.

core_concepts.title: Geomorphology of the Plains (B-T-B-K)
core_concepts.description: From north to south: 1. Bhabar (porous, pebbly belt where streams disappear). 2. Terai (marshy, swampy forest area where streams re-emerge). 3. Bhangar (older alluvium containing calcareous nodules called 'Kankar'). 4. Khadar (newer, highly fertile alluvium renewed every year by floods).

core_concepts.title: The Aravalli Range
core_concepts.description: One of the oldest fold mountains in the world. They are now highly eroded 'relict' mountains. They run from Gujarat to Delhi. The highest peak is 'Guru Shikhar' (in Mount Abu).

core_concepts.title: Vindhyan and Satpura Ranges
core_concepts.description: These are 'Block Mountains' located in central India. The Narmada river flows through a rift valley *between* the Vindhya (north) and Satpura (south) ranges.

core_concepts.title: Peaks of the Peninsula
core_concepts.description: The highest peak in the Western Ghats (and the entire Peninsular India) is 'Anamudi' (in Kerala). The highest peak in the Eastern Ghats is 'Jindhagada Peak' (though older textbooks often cite Mahendragiri).

important_entities.name: Nilgiri Hills
important_entities.significance: The Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats meet at the Nilgiri Hills (Blue Mountains) in Tamil Nadu. The highest peak of the Nilgiris is 'Doddabetta'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A classic trap! Anamudi is the highest peak of South India, located in the Anamalai Hills. Doddabetta is the highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills. Do not confuse the two.
Khadar is NEW alluvium and is much more fertile than Bhangar (OLD alluvium). Remember: 'Khadar' sounds like 'Khaad' (fertilizer).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Vindhya Range -> Narmada River -> Satpura Range -> Tapi River. (This perfectly visualizes the rift valley system).
Bhabar -> Terai -> Bhangar -> Khadar (North to South from the Himalayan foothills).

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the major passes of the Western Ghats: Thalghat (Mumbai-Nashik), Bhorghat (Mumbai-Pune), and Palghat (Kerala-Tamil Nadu).
UPSC frequently tests the definition of 'Doab' (land between two rivers), which is a prominent feature of the Punjab plains.
